messages.subject: Determining which variable is Interm_##
parts:
Hi all, 

When I run a compiled NIMBLE model with a custom sampler and custom functions, I get this following C++ message (though the model runs seemingly fine): 

Run-time size error: expected Interm_2015 - 1 + 1 == TT - Interm_2016 + 1
Run-time size error: expected Interm_2015 - 1 + 1 == TT - Interm_2016 + 1
Run-time size error: expected Interm_2015 - 1 + 1 == TT - Interm_2016 + 1
Problem calling seq in C++ with two indices
Problem calling seq in C++ with two indices

How do I determine which variables/function inputs/etc this refers to?

Here's the general call that happens right before:
nimbleOptions(MCMCusePredictiveDependenciesInCalculations = TRUE) #needed if using custom sampler
  nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)
  nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
  prepbirds <- nimbleModel(code = nimIBM, constants = nc,
                           data = nd, inits = ni, calculate = T, check = T) #goes fast w/ fake data :)
  prepbirds$phi.p[,1] <- 1
  prepbirds$initializeInfo()
  prepbirds$calculate()
  mcmcbirds <- configureMCMC(prepbirds, monitors = pars, print = T, adaptive = TRUE)
  mcmcbirds$removeSampler(c("s", "z", "parent", "age.pre", "k", "phi_HY"))
  mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = c("s", "z", "parent", "age.pre", "phi_HY"),
                       type = "myRWtrajectoryPotentialSampler", silent = F,
                       control = list(scale=SamplerScale, adaptScaleOnly = T, adaptive = TRUE,
                                      npix = nc$npix, pxw = nc$pxw, xmin = nc$xmin, ymin = nc$ymin,
                                      xmax = nc$xmax, ymax = nc$ymax,
                                      gcoords = nc$gcoords, pixels = nd$pixels,
                                      pixcol = nc$pixcol, pixrow = nc$pixrow,
                                      known.z = known.z,
                                      known.parent = known.parent,
                                      known.s = known.s, known.age = known.age,
                                      known.fledge = known.fledge, east = nd$east,
                                      north = nd$north, nocc = nc$nocc, M = nc$M, xoffset = nc$xoffset,
                                      yoffset = nc$yoffset, ntrap = nc$ntrap, nind = nc$nind,
                                      open = nc$open, trap = nc$trap, tune = Tune
                       ))
  mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = "k[1]", type = "RW", control = list(adapative = TRUE, scale = .05))
  mcmcbirds$addSampler(target = "k[2]", type = "RW", control = list(adapative = TRUE, scale = .025))
 
  birdsMCMC <- buildMCMC(mcmcbirds)
 
  Cmodel <- compileNimble(prepbirds) #takes a long time (sometimes)
  Compbirds <- compileNimble(birdsMCMC, project = prepbirds, showCompilerOutput = TRUE)
  out <- runMCMC(Compbirds, niter = 600 , nburnin = 10,inits=ni,
                 setSeed = FALSE, progressBar = TRUE, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)


Thanks!
Heather

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Determining which variable is Interm_##
parts:
Hi Heather,

Sometimes if the source (nimbleFunction or model) code is something like
y[sum(x[1:4])):TT]
the code generated for C++ will do the equivalent of something like
Interm_11 <- sum(x[1:4])
and then use
y[Interm_11:TT],
so the Interm_XX are intermediate variables in some calculation. They are simply numbered in the order in which they are code-generated.

In your case, I would look for something like "<some expression>:TT" that is used as part of some indexing in your code, since the "TT" is likely from your code.

I think the warnings are telling you that some sizes that should match do not actually match. E.g. if you had:
z[1:<some calculation>] <- y[<some calculation>:TT], the lengths of the sequences (e.g. TT - <some calculation> + 1) are not matching.

The specific equation involved could take many forms, so don't get too stuck on my examples but do look for some kind of indexing expression involving "TT".

HTH
Perry
